method: built-precedent research, reference-locked multi-view ImageGen design-source pack, authored metric Blender geometry, physical glass and custom PBR extraction
binding_identity: A welcoming two-storey mass-timber fire station reads as one civic working building through three transparent drive-through apparatus bays, a honey-toned glulam crew wing, a charred service spine, an inhabited channel-glass training tower and a planted photovoltaic roof.

research.role: Built precedent for the charred lower service volume, golden upper wood volume, solid-timber structure and biodiverse rooftop garden.
Marion Fire Station precedent for charred wood, transparent civic presence, occupied terraces and an inhabited training/hose tower.
Mass-timber fire-hall precedent for CLT/glulam clear spans and exactly three double drive-through apparatus lanes.
Built CLT emergency-services precedent confirming mass timber as a real fire-station structural system.

Vehicle-hall precedent for exposed timber frames, glazed folding doors, deep canopy and green-roof construction.

assets.purpose: canonical geometry, material and civic-identity goalpost
prompt_chain:
Create a single photorealistic architectural reference image for a buildable contemporary MASS-TIMBER FIRE STATION, shown in a clean front-left three-quarter view at human eye level with a mild elevated perspective, 16:9 landscape. This is the canonical geometry and material goalpost for a precise 3D model, so make all construction legible and internally consistent.

Building: approximately 40 metres wide by 35 metres deep, two principal storeys, welcoming civic scale rather than a giant industrial shed. Compose it as an articulated but unified building: a low board-formed concrete apparatus base with THREE equal full-height drive-through bays facing the viewer; above and alongside it, a warm honey-toned CLT/glulam crew and community wing with exposed beam ends and deep structural bays; at the left-front corner, an INTEGRATED hose-drying/training stair tower that rises one level above the roof and grows out of the same concrete/timber structural grid, never appearing tacked on. Give the tower a tall translucent channel-glass slot with visible stair landings behind it.

Apparatus facade: three large black-metal framed glass-paneled four-fold overhead doors, each made of multiple realistic transparent panels with physical reflections, mullions, gaskets, door rails and recessed depth. Through the doors, show three correctly scaled red fire engines, concrete floor, timber roof beams, ceiling lights and equipment depth—not flat printed images. Separate the bays with substantial board-formed concrete piers and a continuous timber canopy. Include a clearly identifiable public entrance beside the bays, recessed under a honey-glulam porch with a small civic forecourt.

Upper crew wing: honey-coloured vertical timber rainscreen and exposed glulam columns, broad but deeply recessed high-performance windows with dark frames, real glass material, interior curtains/furniture/light depth, operable vents, and external timber fins/pergola producing strong shadows. Add a roof terrace set behind the timber frame.

Lower service volume: restrained shou sugi ban charred-black vertical timber cladding with tactile grain, balanced against board-formed concrete. Rear/side hints should reveal drive-through depth and service doors.

Roof: extensive planted green roof meadow with varied sedum, native grasses and small wildflowers; a few low shrubs, not trees growing implausibly through the slab. Include two tidy rows of dark photovoltaic panels angled slightly above the planted roof, visible from the camera. The training tower top has a slim metal cap and a small red beacon/antenna.

Site: pale concrete apparatus apron with subtle tire marks and drainage slots, narrow bands of native planting, one restrained station-number marker without readable words, no surrounding city clutter. Soft late-afternoon daylight with crisp natural shadows, realistic PBR material response, detailed architectural photography, 35mm lens, physically plausible dimensions and junctions. Emphasize crafted depth, layered facades, reveals, roof edges, gutters, flashing, structure and occupiable interiors.

Do not create: cartoon, illustration, stylized CGI, toy, LEGO studs, generic rectangular box, sci-fi station, impossible cantilever, distorted fire engines, blank opaque windows, fake printed windows, excessive red cladding, floating stairs, detached tower, text labels, watermarks, people blocking the facade.

Edit the just-generated mass-timber fire station reference image while preserving its camera, lighting, material realism, roof meadow, solar arrays, timber crew wing, concrete-and-channel-glass training tower, and overall architectural character. Correct the apparatus facade so there are EXACTLY THREE and only three glass-paneled overhead fire-engine bay doors. Keep the three visible red engines, one per bay. Remove the apparent fourth/rightmost apparatus door and replace that entire right-hand portion with a clearly solid, lower charred shou-sugi-ban service wing containing only one narrow personnel door and two small deeply recessed service windows. Keep the public entrance to the left of the three bays, under its timber porch. Make the three apparatus doors equal in width and alignment, separated by substantial board-formed concrete piers. Ensure the tower remains physically integrated into the building. Do not add or remove storeys; do not change to cartoon or concept-art styling; no readable signage besides the existing simple number marker.

assets.purpose: rectified front elevation and opening registration

Preserve every identity-defining feature and proportion: integrated concrete/channel-glass training tower on the left; public entrance immediately to its right; exactly THREE equal glass-panel apparatus doors with one red engine visible behind each; solid charred-black service wing on the far right; honey-toned two-storey timber crew wing; exposed glulam columns, beams, balcony/recess depth; green meadow roof; two rows of solar arrays. Camera centered square-on to the front facade with verticals and horizontals perfectly rectified, minimal perspective, full building visible with a narrow apron strip and neutral pale sky. Render as high-end architectural survey photography, accurate PBR materials, realistic glass reflections and occupied interior depth, crisp construction joints and flashing. Do not redesign, add bays, crop the tower, make windows opaque, add text, people, vehicles outside, cartoon styling, diagram labels, or illustration.

assets.purpose: roof topology, drive-through depth and service-plan registration
assets.prompt: Create a photorealistic high oblique aerial / roof reference of the exact SAME mass-timber fire station shown in the two supplied views. Preserve the front composition exactly: integrated left training tower, public entrance, exactly three apparatus bays, solid charred service wing, honey timber crew level. Reveal a plausible 35-metre-deep plan with all THREE apparatus lanes running straight through to three matching rear glass-panel overhead doors; a narrower charred service spine on the right; crew/community rooms wrapping the front and left. Make the extensive green roof a precise build source: varied sedum mat, native grasses and small wildflowers contained behind dark metal parapet flashings, gravel maintenance borders, four roof drains, two orderly photovoltaic arrays on low black racks, one rectangular roof hatch, no implausible trees. Show the tower roof cap and beacon, timber pergola/terrace depth, skylight over the circulation zone, rear concrete service apron, hose connections and restrained mechanical equipment screened by charred timber. Camera from front-left at approximately 35 degrees downward, complete roof and all building edges visible, 16:9 landscape, accurate architectural photography, realistic PBR construction and shadows. Do not redesign facade, add a fourth bay, change materials, add labels, make a diagram, or create stylized CGI.

assets.purpose: rear drive-through, decontamination and service-elevation registration
assets.prompt: Create a photorealistic REAR-RIGHT THREE-QUARTER architectural reference of the exact same mass-timber fire station shown in the supplied front, elevation, and aerial views. Preserve the 40 x 35 m proportions, integrated left-side training tower, honey timber upper crew wing, charred service spine, board-formed concrete, roof meadow and two solar arrays. The rear must logically complete the drive-through station: exactly THREE equal black-framed glass-panel apparatus doors aligned directly behind the three front bays, with partial rear views of the same red engines and real apparatus-hall depth. Provide substantial concrete piers, timber/glulam roof structure visible inside, a broad but thin dark-metal canopy, trench drain and concrete service apron. On the rear crew/service elevations include deeply recessed occupied windows, charred timber service doors, a covered decontamination entrance, hose-drying/service connections, one exterior training landing integrated into the tower, restrained downpipes, wall lights, vents and screened mechanical yard. Keep the tower architecturally embedded, with channel glass revealing real stair flights and landings. Camera squarely reveals rear and right side, 16:9 landscape, late-afternoon architectural photography, realistic physical glass, believable interiors, precise joints, flashing and weathering. Do not add a fourth apparatus bay, a detached staircase, excessive signage, cartoon rendering, labels, people, or unrelated buildings.

assets.purpose: custom honey timber, glulam, charred timber, concrete, green-roof and metal skin source
physical apparatus glazing, crew-window glazing and occupied-depth registration
assets.prompt:
Create a photorealistic two-panel GLASS, WINDOW AND OCCUPIED-DEPTH reference sheet for the exact same mass-timber fire station, split vertically into two equal panels with no labels.

LEFT PANEL: square-on close view of one complete apparatus bay in its board-formed concrete opening. Show a deeply recessed black-metal framed glass four-fold overhead door with multiple horizontal and vertical panels, seals, hinges, track, handle and sill. The glass must be a real material: subtle blue-grey reflection, controlled transmission, varying roughness, slight interior shadows. Behind it show a correctly scaled red fire engine set at least 4 metres back, polished concrete floor with yellow guide line, exposed glulam roof beams, linear lights, hose reel and shelving—crisp enough to read as physical depth but never like a flat poster.

RIGHT PANEL: square-on close view of one upper crew-room timber bay. Show honey glulam posts and beam, deep rain-screen reveal, dark thermally broken frame, separate physical low-E glazing, gasket, sill flashing, operable vent, pale linen curtain offset from the glass, and a softly lit occupied dayroom set behind it with a chair, table, lamp, wall art and ceiling. Include subtle sky/tree reflections without hiding the interior.

Match the exact materials and proportions of the supplied building views. Neutral architectural product photography, high microdetail, physically plausible PBR glass and joinery. No text, labels, people, cartoon look, opaque black windows, printed interiors, mirrored glass, extra bays, logos or watermarks.

assets.purpose: integrated stair, landing, hose-drying and tower-junction registration
assets.prompt: Create a photorealistic two-view CONSTRUCTION DETAIL reference for the integrated training/hose stair tower of the exact same mass-timber fire station. Left half: front-left close three-quarter exterior showing the tower physically interlocked with the board-formed concrete base and glulam crew wing—continuous foundations, shared beam lines, flashing and a recessed joint, never a detached add-on. The tower has pale board-formed concrete side walls, a tall narrow black-framed channel-glass front slot, dark cap and small red beacon. Through the translucent glazing, clearly reveal real alternating stair flights, intermediate landings, guardrails, stringers and warm vertical timber screening at correct floor levels. Include the public entry porch where it meets the tower. Right half: cutaway-like but still photorealistic side view through the glazing, showing concrete stair core, three landings, steel stair/stringers, handrails, hose-drying rack/vertical service zone, wall lights and roof access; all structurally plausible and aligned to the two occupied storeys and tower cap. Neutral architectural photography/product visualization, high construction detail, physically realistic glazing and materials. No labels, arrows, people, floating stair, fake flat window, detached tower, extra storeys, cartoon style or sci-fi forms.
